perspective:
**Brandon Talayumptewa’s accessible information:**

- I am an insurance agent meeting Benjamin Erickson, an entrepreneur seeking business insurance advice. I am aware Benjamin has limited formal education, so I initially worry about explaining complex insurance details effectively.
- First meeting: Benjamin says he wants comprehensive coverage but some terms are new. I explain liability insurance as a safety net, give a slip-and-fall example, and explain asset protection as protecting inventory/equipment. Benjamin asks for an example and about assets, says it makes sense/simplifies things, and thanks me.
- Second meeting: Based on our previous interactions, I have revised my belief that Benjamin can understand detailed information; I feel more confident and plan to discuss complex details. I explain business interruption insurance as covering income loss when unable to operate, and property insurance as covering damage and theft. Benjamin says he is ready, has been reading up, calls business interruption crucial, and says the comprehensive coverage is reassuring.
- Lunch: I feel insecure about how Benjamin perceives my cautious/detail-focused nature, so I try to keep discussions engaging. I tell a joke about an entrepreneur insuring his taste buds. Benjamin says he appreciates my thoroughness but also enjoys lighter moments, and finds the joke fascinating/makes sense considering the stakes. I relate it back to assessing risks.
- Additional support: I feel pleased by Benjamin’s positive response and decide to offer support beyond insurance. I ask if he has considered strategic investments to lower premiums, and suggest security upgrades could reduce insurance costs. Benjamin says he is all ears, calls my insights invaluable, says he hasn’t considered it, calls it smart/win-win, and agrees to explore it.
- Joint venture: Encouraged by strong rapport and mutual benefit, I feel optimistic and propose co-developing a platform integrating risk management with financial planning for entrepreneurs. Benjamin agrees, calls it groundbreaking, says combining our expertise could set us apart, and suggests drafting initial plans. I say we can leverage our strengths for a unique market offering.
